clue.text: Part Belloc used to play in this place

indicators.note: only part of the words Belloc used is taken, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: A role the writer Hilaire Belloc once acted in some venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a theatrical role, but it signals a run of letters inside 'Belloc used'; 'to play in this' is surface padding around the definition 'place'.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a formal or Latin word for a location or site.

clue.text: A lot take an accent to be something attractive

parts.note: loads means a lot
tone is the accent or intonation of the voice

explanation.surface: A crowd adopts a manner of speaking to seem appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is naturally magnetic, a stone that attracts iron.

clue.text: Turned up with duck in relief — it's carved

parts.note: turned up means arrived, came
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A duck appeared in a carved sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal, but it means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a gem or shell carved with a raised figure.

clue.text: The batsmen out

explanation.surface: Two cricketers are dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the strikers are the facing batsmen; workers who are out are on strike.

clue.text: Bottoms as seen in night club entertainment

parts.note: the floors of rooms are their bottoms
'as' and 'how' are interchangeable in 'do as you like' / 'do how you like'

explanation.surface: Rear ends on display in a cabaret act.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret performed on the open dance floor of a nightclub is its standard entertainment.

clue.text: . Watch pockets — cheats appearing

explanation.surface: Thieves seen lifting watches from pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Fobs are small pockets for a watch; to fob off is to cheat or palm someone off.

clue.text: Bowling dominated and made ineffective

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
ridden means dominated, as in guilt-ridden

explanation.surface: A bowler held sway and blunted the batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision overridden is set aside and loses its force.

clue.text: A form of transport

explanation.surface: Some kind of vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In some British schools the Remove is a class or form; to remove is to carry away.

clue.text: How Winnie might be described educationally

definitions.text: How Winnie might be described educationally

parts.words: How Winnie might be described educationally
parts.note: Winnie is Winston Churchill's nickname, and the clue asks what his school makes him

explanation.surface: A question about the schooling of someone called Winnie.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie suggests the Pooh bear; Churchill went to Harrow, an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil or old boy of Harrow School is a Harrovian.

clue.text: Considers small points

parts.note: wee is Scots for small
N and S, north and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up minor details.
explanation.definitionFit: To ween is an archaic verb for to think or suppose.

clue.text: Cracking the French Barmaid mystery

indicators.note: a mystery is a puzzle, so the letters of the barmaid are puzzled into a new order

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Solving a French puzzle about a woman who serves drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mystery' rearranges BARMAID to ADMIRAB, then LE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking is informal British praise meaning excellent, worthy of admiration.

clue.text: Walrus is further round the bend

indicators.note: the word for further is placed round the bend's letter

parts.note: further means more, as in 'no more'
an S-bend is a pipe bend, so S stands for bend

explanation.surface: Someone claims a walrus has gone even madder.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is an old name for the walrus, from Lappish and Russian words for the animal.

clue.text: Sturdy flower, first of the year

parts.note: stock is a scented garden flower

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word year is used

explanation.surface: A robust bloom that appears at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky build is thickset and solidly made.

clue.text: Prior and clergyman in religious surroundings

indicators.note: the word for religious forms surroundings for the clergyman's title

parts.note: pious means devoutly religious
Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A monastic prior and a vicar in a devout setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like the monastic title, in keeping with the clergy, but it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean coming earlier in time, as in a former engagement.

clue.text: It is played in panto — that is, for funny parts

indicators.note: the letters are taken in funny, odd arrangements

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something is acted in pantomime for comic roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny parts' rearranges PANTO, IE and FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the piano, an instrument one plays.

clue.text: Big trouble about angry writer .

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for big

indicators.note: the word for trouble goes about the word for angry

parts.note: care means worry or trouble
wild means furious, angry

explanation.surface: A furious author causes a lot of strife.
explanation.walkthrough: CARE placed about WILD gives CARWILDE, after OS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright and wit who wrote The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Left the close wearing woman's head-dress with a marigold

indicators.note: the head-dress is worn round the words for left and close

parts.note: a caul was a woman's netted cap
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A woman departs the cathedral close in a bonnet with a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' suggests a cathedral close, but it means end.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendula is the botanical genus of the pot marigold.

clue.text: Dance circle lost member

indicators.note: the circle is lost, dropped from the word for the dance

parts.note: the limbo is a Caribbean dance under a lowered bar
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A dance group has had one of its people leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a person in the circle, but it means an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a limb, a member of the body.

clue.text: Having two names gives Mark, no new alibi, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Mark gives a weak excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A binominal name is a two-part scientific name of genus and species.

clue.text: Police dance — just the place for, ready-mades

parts.note: slop is back slang for a policeman, so slops are police
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A police ball is the right place for cheap clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOP is Victorian back slang: 'police' spelt backwards, roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slop shop sold cheap ready-made clothes, called slops.

clue.text: There may be a charge for these fish

definitions.text: There may be a charge for these fish

parts.words: There may be a charge for these fish
parts.note: reads like an admission fee or a price at market, but refers to fish that give an electric shock

explanation.surface: A fishmonger warns that these fish aren't free.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric eels can deliver a strong electric charge to stun prey.

clue.text: Stress — a point with worn foundations

parts.note: to underline a point is to stress it
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Emphasising an argument about buildings with weathered bases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundations' suggests buildings, but here it means foundation garments, underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundation garments are undergarments, and underlinen is an old word for underclothes.

clue.text: Engagement is in a mess

explanation.surface: A betrothal turns out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight one's troth is to promise marriage; a plight is a sorry predicament.

clue.text: Mere existence?

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pond
existence means life

explanation.surface: A philosophical query about a bare, simple life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only', but it is the noun for a lake, so the whole reads as life in a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures that live in ponds are, literally, the life of a mere.

clue.text: Beat with stick

explanation.surface: Hit someone using a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste is slang for to thrash; paste is also glue.

clue.text: What you'd expect of a chimp — a moped crash

definitions.text: What you'd expect of a chimp

indicators.note: after a crash the letters of a moped are left in disorder

explanation.surface: A chimpanzee riding a scooter would surely end up crashing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being an ape is the natural condition, or ape-ness, of a chimpanzee.

clue.text: Spoke at length — for many, a heavy blow

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, many
a welt is a heavy blow or the weal it leaves

explanation.surface: A long speech feels to many like a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on a topic is to speak or write about it at length.

clue.text: Elephantine frenzy from new wine

explanation.surface: Young wine sends someone into a wild rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Must, or musth, is a bull elephant's frenzied state; must is unfermented grape juice.

clue.text: Celebrated without' wife, and got suspended!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for celebrated goes outside

parts.note: a hero is sung, celebrated in song

explanation.surface: A man partied without his spouse and was then barred from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' suggests being barred from work; here it means hung and swayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swung is hung and moved back and forth from a fixed point.

clue.text: Badly cut, perhaps, when chasing a thug

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so this piece follows the word for a thug

parts.note: a rough is a rowdy, a thug

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of when could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone got slashed while pursuing a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges WHEN to HEWN, placed after ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-hewn timber or stone is shaped crudely, without finish.

clue.text: Playfellows square the law

parts.note: to enact a part is to play it
men are fellows
a T-square is a draughtsman's tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Playmates make the rules fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playfellows' splits into two words, Play and fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by parliament is an enactment, a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Pique shown by a novice? That's a bit of a bloomer

parts.note: a pet is a fit of pique or sulking
L is the learner plate on a British car, so stands for novice

explanation.surface: A beginner sulks after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Each petal is one segment of a flower's bloom.
